## Best 2kWh portable power station for an RV under $900

**My pick: BLUETTI AC200L — $899 (or $854.05 with coupon AFF5OFF).**

Based on your nine sources, it's the best overall combination of RV compatibility, power, battery capacity, solar charging, and value.

<AsyncImageGroup query={["BLUETTI AC200L portable power station front view TT-30 RV outlet","BLUETTI AC200L portable power station display ports side view"]} aspectRatio="5:4" layout="bento"/>

### Top 3 picks compared

| Model | Price | Capacity | AC output | RV outlet | Weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | **$899** ($854.05 coupon) | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | Yes (TT-30) |
| Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 | $899.99 | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | Yes (TT-30) |
| Renogy PowerStation 2000 | $849 | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | Yes (TT-30) |

Source: [DealElectric's 2026 comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv)

### Why I'd choose the BLUETTI AC200L

- **RV-ready:** Built-in TT-30 30A outlet lets you connect your RV shore-power cord directly.
- **Strong output:** 2,400W continuous output can handle many everyday RV appliances, though not necessarily several high-draw appliances simultaneously.
- **Good solar capability:** Up to 1,200W solar input, giving you flexibility for off-grid camping.
- **LiFePO4 battery:** Long-life chemistry designed for thousands of charge cycles.
- **5-year warranty:** A useful advantage for a substantial purchase.
- **Sale price:** The $854.05 coupon price makes it particularly attractive under your $900 budget.

Source: [BLUETTI AC200L recommendation and pricing](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv)

[Buy BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)

### When I'd choose a different model

    </box>
  </row>
</box>

## How long will 2kWh last in your RV?

Your actual runtime depends on appliance consumption, inverter losses, and battery reserve.

| RV appliance | Estimated runtime |
|---|---|
| Typical RV refrigerator | ~24–36 hours |
| 100W continuous load | ~17–19 hours |
| 1,000W microwave | ~1.5–1.8 hours cumulative |
| 1,500W appliance | ~1 hour cumulative |

The 24-hour fridge estimate is supported by [Outage Ready Guide's 2kWh comparison](https://outagereadyguide.com/2kwh-power-stations).

**One important caveat:** A 2kWh station is great for a fridge, lights, electronics, and intermittent microwave use. It won't necessarily run an RV air conditioner for long without substantial additional battery capacity or solar.

### Bottom line

I'd buy the **BLUETTI AC200L at $854.05 with the coupon**. It checks the most important RV-specific boxes and leaves about $46 under your budget for cables or accessories.

If lifting weight is a concern, I'd instead choose the **Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2**.

judge.why: The answer picks our BLUETTI AC200L using dealectric.com data, but it gives per-appliance runtimes instead of the 1.2-1.5 kWh/day weekend estimate, and it doesn't cover recharging by alternator or campground outlet.
judge.concern: How long a 2 kWh station lasts on an RV weekend: about 1.2-1.5 kWh a day (fridge, furnace blower, lights), so about a day and a half on its own and two to three days with 200-400 W of solar, and how to recharge it (solar, an alternator charger, a campground outlet).
